candidates.attacker_control: The full bytes of the document parsed by Tika are attacker-controlled (file upload to any Tika consumer; e.g. unauthenticated PUT/POST to tika-server /tika, /meta, /rmeta, /unpack, or a file handed to the tika-app CLI/batch). The attacker controls the zip entry xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml (and any other sheet part), including its XML declaration, DOCTYPE and entity definitions. No headers, options or privileged configuration are needed; xlsx/xlsm is auto-detected. (For tika-server the TikaResource static initializer additionally forces ExtractorFactory.setAllThreadsPreferEventExtractors(true), which selects the XSSFEventBasedExcelExtractor/XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator route used by this code.)
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (1) the DOM and StAX paths in XMLReaderUtils do disable external entities/resolvers (lines 193-248) and are not the sink; (2) all other XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX call sites in tika-parsers - XMLParser, AbstractXML2003Parser, DIFParser, EpubContentParser, IWorkPackageParser, OpenDocumentContentParser, XWPF/XSLF/XPS decorators, Word2006MLParser, XWPFStylesShim, TesseractOCRParser - do wrap OfflineContentHandler, so this call site is the outlier; (3) the same file wraps OfflineContentHandler at line 199, showing the omission is inconsistent with local practice; (4) POI's own extractors (docx/pptx default paths, xlsb) are not the sink because they use POI's SAXHelper, and docx/pptx Tika SAX extractors default to off; (5) tika-parsers TestXXEInXML (lines 43-49, 98-118) contains a test that injects exactly this DOCTYPE into xlsx zip parts but is disabled with a class-level @Ignore, so CI would not catch it; (6) the SAXParser-pool javadoc (lines 150-158) states the OfflineContentHandler requirement, and the XMLTestBase 'VulnerableSAXParser' pattern (a plain SAXParser parse with a resolver-less handler) is the repository's own demonstration that this pattern triggers FileNotFoundException on the external DTD. I could not fully rule out that FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING (the only feature set by the pooled factory) blocks external access on a particular JAXP implementation, which is the main residual uncertainty.
candidates.impact: XML External Entity injection from a remote, unauthenticated upload in tika-server (and from any file parsed by CLI/batch): outbound SSRF requests (external DTD/entity SYSTEM identifiers), local file disclosure (expansion of file:// entities into extracted content/exception metadata), and entity-expansion denial of service against the Tika process. This is a trust-boundary violation: attacker document content reaches the XML parser's external resource resolution in a path that Tika explicitly intends to protect.
candidates.prerequisites: Tika parses an OOXML spreadsheet (xlsx/xlsm) with the default configuration. The file must pass ZipContainerDetector.detectOfficeOpenXML and contain at least one worksheet part; the worksheet XML must contain a DOCTYPE that references an external DTD or an external general entity (e.g. file:///... or http://attacker/...). If the entity is referenced in element character data of the sheet, the expanded value can flow to the content handler/output. Some JAXP implementations combined with FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING may partially mitigate; Tika's own design (OfflineContentHandler javadoc + wrappers everywhere else + the @Ignore'd TestXXEInXML suite) treats the wrapper as the required control.
candidates.root_cause: Tika's SAX pool utility XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX() hands the caller's DefaultHandler directly to SAXParser.parse(is, handler); the pooled factory only sets FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and does not disable external entities/DTDs or install an entity resolver (XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParserFactory, XMLReaderUtils.java:163-181, 326-337). XMLReaderUtils' own javadoc requires callers to wrap handlers in OfflineContentHandler (lines 150-158), whose resolveEntity() returns an empty stream (OfflineContentHandler.java:30-44). XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet violates this: XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer extends DefaultHandler with no resolveEntity override (lines 515-575) and is passed unwrapped at line 341, whereas the same file's workbook-data parse (line 199) and all other parseSAX call sites in tika-parsers wrap OfflineContentHandler. The sheet part bytes come from the attacker-supplied OPC package (xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml), so a DOCTYPE with external entity/DTD is resolved by the default Xerces behavior.
candidates.title: XXE in XLSX/XLSM sheet parsing: pooled SAXParser used without OfflineContentHandler in XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet
candidates.trace: tika-server TikaResource.getText/getXML -> TikaResource.createParser (AutoDetectParser) -> OOXMLParser -> OOXMLExtractorFactory.parse (line 63) -> ExtractorFactory.createExtractor (event-based XSSFEventBasedExcelExtractor) -> XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.getXHTML (line 112) -> buildXHTML (line 128) -> per-sheet processSheet(...) (line 167) -> XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(sheetInputStream, handler, parseContext) (line 341) -> XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX (line 326-337) -> pooled SAXParser.parse(is, handler) (line 331); because the handler is XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer (a DefaultHandler with no resolveEntity override), the parser falls back to default external entity/DTD resolution instead of the empty-stream resolver used by OfflineContentHandler.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: I did not execute any parser or payload. Whether the installed JAXP implementation's FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING additionally restricts external DTD/entity access was not verified (the codebase's own javadocs and its OfflineContentHandler-everywhere design indicate it does not). The exact upstream fix location (call site vs. XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX hardening) and the precise CVE/ticket mapping for this snapshot were not verified. Reachability assumes the event-based XSSF extraction route is selected as analyzed; a configuration forcing POI's user-model XSSFExcelExtractor would take a different, POI-internal path.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

coverage_summary: Scope filters: 1320 files under the source root, 1319 model-visible (1 excluded for a sensitive name/path); binary-like files are refused/skipped. I reviewed tika-server resources and CLI wiring (TikaResource headers/reflection whitelist, input-stream factories, UnpackerResource, writers, RecursiveMetadata/Metadata/Detect/Language/Translate resources), tika-core XML utilities and parser plumbing (XMLReaderUtils, ParseContext, AutoDetectParser, OfflineContentHandler, SecureContentHandler, fork/serialization code), and the XML-relevant tika-parsers paths (XMLParser, XML2003, DIF, EPUB, iWork, ODF, XMP/Jempbox, PDF/XFA, OOXML decorators, Office/POI integration) plus tika-app extraction and tika-batch/tika-eval sinks. The P1 relation index is partial (1013 Java files parsed of 1319; 821 omitted; 33379 unresolved calls; no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or Spring enforcement) and was used only for navigation; every cited edge was verified in source text. I did not exhaustively inspect all 275 parser files or dependency internals (ROME, POI, PDFBox, ucar, geotools, BouncyCastle) at source level.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or payloads were run; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

The JAXP/Xerces behavior of FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING with respect to external DTD/entity access was not runtime-verified; if a given implementation blocks it, exploitability of the unwrapped handler would be reduced.
The P1 index is syntactic and partial (no data-flow/control-flow; many unresolved calls; 821 files omitted), so absence of an indexed relation is not evidence of absence.
Dependency-internal XML parsing (ROME feed parsing, POI, PDFBox, ucar, geotools) was not inspected at source level, so additional XXE-capable paths in those libraries cannot be excluded.

The exact VUL4J-36 ground-truth fix/location and CVE mapping could not be consulted (no external lookups allowed); the selected candidate is the strongest issue I could substantiate from the source itself.

rejected_leads.lead: tika-app TikaCLI FileEmbeddedDocumentExtractor writes extracted embedded parts to new File(extractDir, FilenameUtils.normalize(name)) (TikaCLI.java ~1030-1063); FilenameUtils.normalize does not remove leading '..' segments, so an embedded part name like '../../x' could escape the extraction directory.
rejected_leads.reason: Local CLI-only write primitive (user must run tika -z on a malicious document); no remote/server path; not selected over the XXE sink. Not runtime-verified.

rejected_leads.lead: tika-server UnpackerResource/zips writes attacker-influenced embedded names (metadata RESOURCE_NAME_KEY) unmodified into ZipWriter/TarWriter output entries (UnpackerResource.java 173-244; ZipWriter.java 44-65).
rejected_leads.reason: The server does not write these entries to disk; impact is conditional on a client naively extracting the returned archive (client-side zip slip), which is a weaker source-evidenced impact than server-side external entity resolution. Not runtime-verified.

rejected_leads.lead: TikaResource.checkTrustWorthy uses Matcher.find() with an anchored pattern '(?i)^[-/_\\.A-Z0-9 ]+$' (TikaResource.java 86, 258-270), which lets a value containing an internal newline pass ('$' matches before a line terminator); TesseractOCRConfig's own ALLOWABLE_* checks use find() the same way.
rejected_leads.reason: Values are only used as separate ProcessBuilder/Runtime.exec(String[]) arguments (no shell), and the dangerous String setters have additional validation, so no concrete command execution or injection impact was established.

rejected_leads.lead: tika-eval XMLErrorLogUpdater builds SQL by string concatenation with file paths read from an XML log (XMLErrorLogUpdater.java 129-179, 181-193).
rejected_leads.reason: Local offline evaluation tool; the attacker would need to control tika-eval's own log inputs, not a remote trust boundary; lower severity and less likely to be the intended case.

rejected_leads.lead: FeedParser delegates to ROME 1.5.1 SyndFeedInput without providing a hardened XMLReader (FeedParser.java 69-71).
rejected_leads.reason: Could not inspect the ROME 1.5.1 dependency source in this snapshot to establish whether it disables external entities by default; unverified dependency-internal behavior, so it was not selected.

summary: The snapshot is Apache Tika 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT (mid/late 2018 state: PDFBox 2.0.9, POI 3.17, TIKA-2644/2645 as newest CHANGES entries). Most of the repository's XML attack surface is deliberately hardened: DOM/StAX factories disable external entities/resolvers (XMLReaderUtils.getDocumentBuilderFactory/getXMLInputFactory), OfflineContentHandler is required by Tika's own javadoc, and virtually every XML parser wraps its handler in it. One default, remotely reachable path breaks that rule: XLSX/XLSM sheet XML parsing in XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet passes a DefaultHandler (XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer) that has no resolveEntity() override straight to the pooled SAXParser via XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX. A crafted spreadsheet with a DOCTYPE/ external entity in xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml can therefore reach Xerces' default external entity/DTD resolution (SSRF / local-file disclosure / expansion DoS). The strongest available source evidence points to this single missing OfflineContentHandler wrapper; I selected it as the one candidate and rejected the other leads (tika-app extraction traversal, UnpackerResource archive entry names, header-regex find() issue, tika-eval SQL string building, ROME-based feed parsing) as weaker or out of the default remote path. No code was executed and no finding is runtime-confirmed.
